title: VacationSchedule — Free Time Scoreboard (SF Radio Blackout Calendar)
description: Bay Area vacation planner comparing three definitions of sports-free time in 2026-2029 for a listener in San Francisco ZIP 94122, with one-, two- and three-week trip checks, a daily scoreboard, a month calendar, Pacific-time free intervals, sources and a review queue. The three sections nest: Section 1 counts all 30 MLB clubs plus 49ers preseason, regular season and postseason and the Westwood One national NFL feeds as busy; Section 2 adds Stanford and California football; Section 3 adds San Jose Earthquakes MLS. An 'Everything tracked' option adds national NCAA football plus Golden State Warriors and Golden State Valkyries on KGMZ 95.7 The Game. Only AM/FM broadcasts count, so the San Jose Sharks (app/streaming only) and Audacy-app-only Valkyries games are disclosed exclusions, and USF basketball, Westwood One NCAA basketball and local college basketball are named as documented gaps rather than silently treated as free time. With Spring Training excluded, Sections 1 and 2 give longest modeled windows of 44 days in 2026 (Feb 9 - Mar 24, past), 37 in 2027 (Feb 15 - Mar 23), 40 in 2028 (estimated) and 41 in 2029 (estimated); with Spring Training included no section reaches two weeks. The repository refuses a blanket verified claim: TBD kickoff reserves the entire local date including DST 23- and 25-hour days, 'no known conflict' is stated to describe the snapshot rather than certify a quiet day, and all times are America/Los_Angeles rather than a fixed UTC-8 offset. A 2026-09-21 session-3 pass added two tabs: MLB 2026 & 2027, listing every fixture the league has scheduled for all 30 clubs from the committed Stats API snapshot with each row carrying the league's own game_pk, and Postseason 2026, which splits the postseason into what is resolved and what is not — clinched berths and division titles, official round dates, dates that cannot carry a game, and a machine-measured count of published first pitches, still zero. The fixture lists are produced on a GitHub runner by scripts/export_mlb_schedule.py, validated for all 30 clubs, a plausible regular-season count and unique game ids, and committed with a provenance summary recording the exact request URL, the retrieval time and a SHA-256 of the raw response, so every row is re-verifiable by hand. Where a season snapshot exists the analysis blocks real fixture dates rather than a continuous season frame. The 125-test suite was executed here and passes.
